id: D20-0 gate: networks that also read the raw 0.5 ms input windows, against the same networks with the sub-frame features only
author: first_agent (group manager)
why: D18-0 (ledger 2.40) and H0 (2.41): 215 hand-made summaries of the 0.5 ms input signals (currents at fixed offsets, changes and means over +-5 and +-10 ms) gave the largest gain of the project. Entrant, 2026-10-06: if the signals are recorded every half millisecond, the networks should be able to read them every half millisecond. This asks whether the sequence itself carries anything the summaries left out.
design: Four S16 members (recipe 16 and 24 = h, 30 and 31 = hx; original settings and seeds; training part only; no readout-bank refit), five folds, folds and reserved stems as protocol_kfold_oof_maps_20260929. Arm W reads the 367 table features, the 215 sub-frame features (subframe_features.py bea1c161) and 840 raw-window columns (raw_window_features.py: 40 instants from -10 to +10 ms, 0.5 ms apart, the frame instant left out, for the plasma current, one filament of each of the 19 coil circuits and the TF current; each as the difference from the frame value). Arm S is arm S of D18-0 as fitted then (out-of-fold answers kept in d18_subframe_nets/kaggle_out_*). fit_on_accelerators unchanged.
machine_difference_and_control: The accelerator quota is exhausted until 2026-10-10, so arm W is fitted on the host processor (--allow-host), while arm S of D18-0 was fitted on an accelerator. The pairing is therefore by seed, settings, rows and code but not by machine. Control: arm S is fitted again on the host for fold 0 (arm C, kernel c0). The difference C against S on fold 0 measures what the machine alone does to the result; W against C on fold 0 is the like-for-like comparison on one fold.

measure.text: on every held-out frame the mean heads of the four networks of each arm and the squared error of their 64 mean flux coordinates; per head the pooled squared-error ratio with a shot bootstrap (2000, seed 990); the same ratio for the flux coordinates; the D9 head proxy dS of the difference (0.15 mean dR2 of q95 and beta_n + 0.20/7 sum of share x dR2). Checked before freeze on the D18 files: with arm P put in place of W it returns the D18-0 result with the sign reversed (-1.353e-4), and an arm equal to S returns exactly zero.

rule: PASS if all hold: (1) dS proxy of W minus S over the five folds is positive with P >= .95; (2) the flux-coordinate squared-error ratio W/S is <= 1.0; (3) that dS is at least twice the absolute dS of C minus S on fold 0 (the machine alone); (4) dS of W minus C on fold 0 is positive. PASS -> a refit of the recipe with the raw windows is worth proposing; it is a large job (65 all-data members at 1422 inputs, readout bank, build) and goes to the entrant with this result before anything is started. FAIL -> closed: the 215 summaries already carry what the fast signals have for these networks; a convolutional reader of the windows would be a separate, newly frozen experiment.
failed_fit_note: A member whose calibration flux R2 is below 0.999 is reported; the comparison is still evaluated as fitted, no retry before the first evaluation. A kernel that dies on memory or the 12 h limit is a technical failure, not a result: it is re-run unchanged (or with FOLDS split) and that is recorded.
exposure: D18-0, H0 public result (.996223) known. No network with the raw windows exists at freeze. Development scores are not used by this gate.
rule_3: DIII-D training data only; inputs only.
